questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ethernet MAC address.
I. It is 32 bits long.
II. It is written as eight pairs of hexadecimal digits.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. A MAC address is 48 bits (six bytes), written as six pairs of hexadecimal digits. Eight pairs would make 64 bits.

questions.q: Which protocol is used by hosts and routers to manage membership of multicast groups?
questions.e: IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol) lets a host tell its local router which multicast groups it wants to join.

questions.q: Classic wired Ethernet (IEEE 802.3) uses which medium access method?
questions.e: Ethernet senses the carrier and detects collisions. CSMA/CA is used in wireless LANs (IEEE 802.11).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The data link layer provides node-to-node delivery of frames.
II. The transport layer provides process-to-process delivery.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Data link delivery is hop-by-hop between adjacent nodes, while the transport layer uses port numbers to deliver data between processes. Both are correct.

questions.q: Which IP address is the loopback address used for testing the local TCP/IP stack?
questions.e: Addresses in the block 127.0.0.0/8 loop back to the same host. 127.0.0.1 is the standard one.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. UDP is a connectionless protocol.
II. TCP provides flow control and reliable delivery.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: UDP sends datagrams without setting up a connection. TCP uses acknowledgements, retransmission and a sliding window. Both statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. ARP maps a MAC address to an IP address.
II. RARP maps an IP address to a MAC address.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The two are swapped. ARP maps IP to MAC, and RARP maps MAC to IP. Neither statement is correct.

questions.q: In ______ mode, communication can take place in both directions, but only one direction at a time.
questions.e: Half duplex alternates directions, as in a walkie-talkie. Full duplex allows both directions at once.

questions.q: In VoIP, the speech signal is digitised and carried over an IP network as ______.
questions.e: VoIP breaks digitised voice into small packets sent with protocols such as RTP over UDP. It does not need a dedicated circuit.

questions.q: How many usable host addresses are available in each subnet of a /26 network?
questions.e: A /26 leaves 32 − 26 = 6 host bits, so 2⁶ = 64 addresses. Subtracting the network and broadcast addresses gives 62.

questions.q: A noiseless channel of bandwidth 4000 Hz carries a signal with 8 levels. By the Nyquist formula, the maximum bit rate is
questions.e: Nyquist bit rate = 2 × B × log₂L = 2 × 4000 × log₂8 = 2 × 4000 × 3 = 24000 bps.

questions.q: A channel has bandwidth 3000 Hz and signal-to-noise ratio 1023 (not in dB). By Shannon's formula its capacity is
A signal of frequency 3 GHz travels at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in free space. Its wavelength is
In the stop-and-wait protocol, the propagation time equals the transmission time of a frame (a = Tp/Tt = 1). The link efficiency is
questions.e: Efficiency = 1 / (1 + 2a) = 1 / 3, which is about 33.3%.

questions.q: With a 3-bit sequence number field, the maximum sender window size in the Go-Back-N protocol is
questions.e: Go-Back-N needs window ≤ 2ⁿ − 1 = 7. A window of 8 would make a new frame indistinguishable from a retransmission.

questions.q: A CRC uses the generator polynomial x³ + x + 1. How many redundant bits are appended to the data?
questions.e: The generator has degree 3, so 3 zeros are appended and the 3-bit remainder replaces them. The generator itself is the 4-bit pattern 1011.

questions.q: How many parity bits are needed to correct a single-bit error in 7 data bits using Hamming code?
questions.e: The condition is 2ʳ ≥ m + r + 1. For m = 7, r = 3 gives 8 ≥ 11, which fails, but r = 4 gives 16 ≥ 12, which works.

questions.q: The minimum Hamming distance required in a code to correct up to 2 bit errors is
questions.e: To correct t errors the code needs distance 2t + 1. For t = 2 that is 5.

questions.q: The Internet checksum used by IP, TCP and UDP is computed using
questions.e: The sender adds the 16-bit words in one's complement arithmetic and complements the sum. The receiver repeats this and checks for all ones.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The maximum throughput of pure ALOHA is about 36.8%.
II. The maximum throughput of slotted ALOHA is about 18.4%.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The values are swapped. Pure ALOHA peaks at 1/(2e) ≈ 18.4%, slotted ALOHA at 1/e ≈ 36.8%.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the TCP three-way handshake.
I. The first segment is a SYN+ACK sent by the server.
II. The last segment is an ACK sent by the client.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only II is correct. The client sends SYN first, the server replies with SYN+ACK, and the client completes the handshake with ACK.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about DHCP.
I. The DHCP server listens on UDP port 67.
II. The DHCP client uses UDP port 68.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. DHCP runs over UDP, with port 67 at the server and port 68 at the client. Port 53 belongs to DNS.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about OSPF is NOT correct?
o: Routers compute shortest paths using the Bellman-Ford algorithm
It is a link-state routing protocol
It is an interior gateway protocol
Each router builds a map of its area
questions.e: OSPF routers run Dijkstra's shortest path first algorithm on the link-state map. Bellman-Ford is used by distance-vector protocols such as RIP.
